docTitle: Wingetarium · the winget catalogue, fresh every day
metaDesc: What’s in the official winget repository: hand-picked packages with today’s version, search across all packages, the key commands and what winget can’t do. Updated every morning, no cookies, works offline.
dek: What’s really in the official winget repository: {n} hand-picked packages with today’s version, a search across all {all} packages, the commands you actually need, and the honest list of what winget can’t do. The numbers come fresh from the original index every morning.
what1: winget isn’t a store with its own files. It’s an address book: for every package there’s a YAML file in the repo that says where the installer lives on the vendor’s site, which SHA256 hash it must have and which switches install it silently.
what2: So with winget install your PC downloads straight from Mozilla, Valve or Microsoft, not from some mirror server. If the hash doesn’t match, winget stops. That’s exactly what makes it safer than a download from a random software site.
what3: New packages go through automated checks before they’re accepted: Microsoft SmartScreen, static analysis and SHA256 verification.
srcWinget: The community repository with the {n} packages above. Maintained by vendors and volunteers, checked by Microsoft. Practically everything comes from here.
srcStore: The Microsoft Store. Useful for Store exclusives, but the first time it asks you to accept the Store terms, and paid apps need a signed-in account.

grow: When version 1.0 launched in May 2021, the repo held about 1,400 packages. On 22 September 2026 I counted 14,940, today it’s {n}. If you can’t find something, it’s worth checking again in a few months.

limitsIntro: The numbers here come from today’s index and are recounted every morning.
lGpu: No GeForce or Radeon display driver in the repo. Under Nvidia.* there are only side pieces like CUDA, PhysX, FrameView and firmware updaters. You still get your graphics driver from the card’s maker.
lGpuFound: Today there actually is a display driver in the repo: {list}. That’s new, there’s never been one before.
lDriver: {n} packages have “Driver” in their name, but they’re ODBC, printer and card reader drivers. winget doesn’t do general driver updates.
lGames: winget installs Steam, Epic, GOG, EA and Ubisoft as launchers. The games inside are up to each client.
lFonts: Only {n} packages have anything to do with fonts at all, and most are tools like FontForge. Real font families are rare; exceptions are DEVCOM.JetBrainsMonoNerdFont and SourceFoundry.HackFonts.
lAuto: winget doesn’t update anything on its own. Someone has to run winget upgrade --all: you, or a task in Task Scheduler.
lSource: No equivalent of make or the AUR build scripts. winget downloads finished installers, nothing else.
lFormats: No .tar.gz, .7z or .rar, no self-extracting archives, nothing without a silent install mode and nothing that only exists for ARM32.
lGaps: Some things are simply missing. {list} isn’t in the repo today. Even well-known software is no guarantee.
lGood: WSL including Ubuntu 24.04, the complete Sysinternals suite, Visual Studio 2022, JDKs in every flavour, Windows SDKs and even Anthropic.Claude plus Anthropic.ClaudeCode.
ytTitle: About yt-dlp and the YouTube wrappers in the picks
yt: The packages are clean and free of malware, that’s not the point. But downloading around YouTube and clients that block ads violate the YouTube Terms of Service, and Google has been actively going after such apps since 2025. That’s why they break regularly. For your own recordings and public-domain material, yt-dlp is a great tool, but not as a long-term way to listen to music.
how: Every morning a GitHub workflow downloads the official source index from cdn.winget.microsoft.com/cache/source.msix, which contains an SQLite database with the complete catalog, and writes the figures on this page from it. It takes the descriptions from the manifests of packages that changed since the day before. Index as of: {d}. Your browser only ever talks to this site, never to Microsoft. Every package ID in the selection is checked against the index on each run.
